hx_gen_derivative_filter — 2D halcon_ext op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "hx_gen_derivative_filter", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: gen_derivative_filter (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Usage

A derivative filter in the frequency domain. a is the order of the derivative, b its direction.

HALCON's gen_derivative_filter takes a Derivative (x / y / xx / yy / xy) and an order, but for a long time this op merely normalised and returned |f|, looking at neither the input content nor the knobs at all -- measured on 2026-09-02: for the same shape, changing a/b or passing a different picture gave a byte-identical result (the siblings hx_gen_lowpass / hx_gen_highpass / hx_gen_bandfilter change with their knobs, so this 1 op alone stood out).

• a : order 1 to 2 (|f| or |f|^2). Order 2 corresponds to the Laplacian.

• b : orientation. 0 gives the x direction |f_x|, 1 the y direction |f_y|, and in between it blends smoothly toward the isotropic |f| (exactly isotropic at 0.5).

The result is the filter itself in the frequency domain (the same convention as HALCON's gen_*), so the input is used only to determine the shape. However, it now actually changes with the knobs, not just with the shape, so evolution can choose the order and orientation.

Value comparability (measured): the output is normalised by that image's own maximum (the output maximum is always 1.0, and scaling the input leaves the output unchanged). Values therefore cannot be compared across images — a feature of the same strength takes a different value depending on what the strongest feature in that image happens to be, and in an image holding only weak features the noise is lifted to 1.0. To compare across images, rescale by a common reference.
